subject: Art & Design
title: Garamond: The 500-Year-Old Masterpiece
description: Learn Garamond: The 500-Year-Old Masterpiece in one minute.

hook.text: Claude Garamond designed his typeface in the 1530s. It's still in use today — nearly 500 years of continuous service.

buildup.text: Garamond was one of the first typefaces designed for print rather than mimicking handwriting.

discovery.text: Its elegant proportions, low contrast, and open counters make it supremely readable in long texts.

twist.text: A 2014 study claimed switching US government documents to Garamond would save $136 million in ink yearly.

climax.text: Garamond is the default for academic publishing, literary novels, and luxury print — timeless and trusted.

punchline.text: Some designs don't age. Garamond is proof.

quiz.question: Why is Garamond considered exceptionally readable?
options: Elegant proportions, low contrast, and open letter shapes
It uses very large letter sizes
It was designed by a computer algorithm

details.summary: Garamond, originating from 16th-century punch-cutter Claude Garamond's designs, is one of the oldest typeface families still in widespread use. Its elegant, readable letterforms with gentle contrast and minimal decoration have made it a standard for book typography for over 500 years.
details.whyItMatters: Garamond's longevity proves that foundational design quality transcends trends and technology. A typeface designed for metal printing in the 1500s remains one of the most readable and beautiful choices for digital screens and print in the 2020s.
takeaways: One of the oldest typefaces still in widespread professional use
Its readability and elegance have endured over 500 years

faq.question: Could switching to Garamond really save millions in ink?
faq.answer: A 2014 student study estimated the US government could save $400 million by switching from Times New Roman to Garamond, which uses thinner strokes. While the methodology was questioned — the comparison used different sizes — the principle is valid: lighter typefaces use measurably less ink at scale.

faq.question: Which version of Garamond should I use?
faq.answer: Adobe Garamond Pro is the most faithful to the original designs and excellent for body text. EB Garamond is a free, high-quality open-source option. Apple Garamond and ITC Garamond are stylistic variations. For serious typographic work, Adobe Garamond Pro is generally the professional standard.
